preamble: Fifteen clues contain a thematic word that must be replaced by a sixteenth common one of the same kind (as suggested by the unclued solutions for 12 and 27 across).

solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; each light's entry one fifteensquared prints for it, the only choice of them whose crossings all agree; an entry not its answer carries the answer as its alteration's `from`

clue.text: Bishop quickly photographs church interior

definitions.note: the thematic drink word: read it as gin, of which schnaps is a Dutch kind

indicators.note: the church is said to be the inside part, so it sits within the other word

explanation.surface: A cleric hurriedly snaps pictures inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Bishop is a mulled port drink, one of the fifteen drinks the preamble swaps for gin; read the clue as 'Gin quickly photographs church interior' and SCHNAPS appears as S(CH)NAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnaps, or schnapps, is a name for strong Dutch gin as well as other spirits.

clue.text: Surprisingly can vote in foreign capital? It's of little value

definitions.text: in foreign capital? It's of little value

indicators.note: a surprising outcome is an unexpected one, so these letters come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: An unexpected chance to vote in a foreign city turns out to count for little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like a city but means money; the definition runs from 'in foreign capital' to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A centavo is a small coin worth one hundredth of the peso or real in several Latin American currencies.

clue.text: Throw china around, missing a town in Cheshire

indicators.note: thrown around, the letters are scattered into a new order
missing means going without, so one letter is lost from the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone hurling crockery about, and missing, somewhere in Cheshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing a' does double duty: the A drops out of the fodder before the shuffle, leaving nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Northwich is a salt-mining town in mid Cheshire, a county in north-west England.

clue.text: Language Sherry used after short swim, when upset

indicators.note: a short version of the word for a swim loses its final letter
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: a dip is a quick swim; short, it loses its last letter (DIPS shortened)
the thematic drink word, to be read as gin per the preamble

explanation.surface: A woman named Sherry speaks some tongue after an upsetting dip.
explanation.walkthrough: Sherry is one of the fifteen drink words to be replaced by gin. A swim is a dip (or dips, cut short), which reversed in this down clue gives PID, followed by GIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A pidgin is a simplified contact language used between speakers with no common tongue.

clue.text: Time of year to start on elderberry wine

definitions.note: the thematic drink word: read it as gin, in its sense of a snare

indicators.note: the start of the fruit's name is its opening letter only

explanation.surface: The season to begin making elderberry wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Wine is a thematic word: read 'gin', and gin is also a trap for catching game.
explanation.definitionFit: A springe is a noose or snare for small game, and a gin is likewise a trap or snare.

clue.text: Notices clue brought up refuelling breaks

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up means reading it from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: Signs giving hints are raised during motor-race stops.
explanation.definitionFit: Pit stops are pauses in a motor race for fuel and tyres, or informally any break on a journey.

clue.text: Some target meal without starter

indicators.note: a starter here is a first letter, and without it the word loses its opening

explanation.surface: Part of a dinner plan skipping the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' sounds like a first course of the meal, but it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner is the ring round the bull on an archery or shooting target, so it is one portion of it.

clue.text: Tell Stella about something hung vertically to catch fish

definitions.text: something hung vertically to catch fish

indicators.note: turned about, the letters are moved round into a new order

parts.note: the thematic drink word, a brand of lager, to be read as gin

explanation.surface: Telling a woman called Stella about some fishing gear.
explanation.walkthrough: Stella (Artois) is a lager and one of the fifteen drink words; with gin in its place, TELL and GIN are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A gill net hangs upright in the water so that fish swimming into it are caught by the gills.

clue.text: Study really briefly in state capital

indicators.note: said briefly, the word is cut short and loses its end

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room for work

explanation.surface: A very quick spell of studying somewhere in a state capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Denver is the seat of government of Colorado, the Mile High City in the Rocky Mountain region of the United States.

clue.text: Name of situation where solutions might be wrongly alcohol-free

indicators.note: something done wrongly is out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the thematic drink word, to be read as gin
rid means free, as in rid of a burden

explanation.surface: A cryptic hint at where crossword answers go, and a liquor-free name.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle is a cryptic gloss: answers are written IN GRID. The wordplay is 'wrongly gin-free', a scrambled GIN followed by RID.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrid is a woman's given name, made famous by the actress Ingrid Bergman.

clue.text: Catch fish after casting net

indicators.note: casting throws the letters out so that they land in a new order

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: An angler lands a fish after throwing a net.
explanation.definitionFit: To entangle is to snare or trap something so it cannot get free, which is to catch it.

clue.text: Old cricketer caught in Alaskan hailstorm

indicators.note: the name is held inside the following words, caught within them

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A former batsman trapped in a storm in Alaska.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' is a cricket term in the surface, but here it marks the hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rohan Kanhai was a celebrated West Indies batsman of the 1950s to 1970s.

clue.text: Ex-servicemen have to check before returning it?

indicators.note: returning means going back, so this word is read from right to left

parts.note: it, Italian vermouth, is the thematic word; read as gin, a trap or snare

explanation.surface: Old soldiers must have something examined before sending it back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is the vermouth of gin and it. Swapped for gin, it means a snare, which reversed follows VET.
explanation.definitionFit: Veterans are former members of the armed forces, especially those who saw active service.

clue.text: When conversing, Philip is a fine mixer

indicators.note: in conversation words are heard rather than read, so the name stands for its sound

parts.note: the name is pronounced the same as fillip, a boost or stimulus
fine is the thematic word, a brandy; as gin, a mixer that goes with it

explanation.surface: Philip mixes well in conversation and is good company.
explanation.walkthrough: Fine (a French brandy) is the thematic word; with gin in its place, the second meaning is a gin mixer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is a fillip, something that boosts or invigorates, and tonic water is the classic mixer for gin.

clue.text: Brother keeping quiet, reportedly drunk on vodka?

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another comes after it, so the word for drunk goes second

parts.note: the thematic word; read as gin, in its sense of a trap

indicators.note: reported speech is heard, so the word is spelt as it sounds

parts.note: a slang word for drunk, said out loud

explanation.surface: A monk sworn to silence who is said to be drunk on vodka.
explanation.walkthrough: Vodka is replaced by gin, which here means a trap. In an across clue 'on' puts the second piece after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappist monks belong to a Cistercian order known for its rule of silence, and a monk is a brother.

clue.text: Dinosaur upsetting Una in Dog & Duck

indicators.note: upsetting things knocks them over and out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A dinosaur causing a stir by upsetting a woman in the Dog and Duck pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dog & Duck looks like a single pub name, but it is split into its parts, with Duck as O.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguanodon was a large plant-eating dinosaur of the Cretaceous period.

clue.text: Some imbibe arak nervously, as a novice

indicators.note: only some of each word is kept, the stretch that runs on into the next

parts.note: the thematic word, an aniseed spirit, to be read as gin

explanation.surface: A newcomer anxiously sipping some arak.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a hidden word in the setter's intent, but the letters only run through the clue once arak, a thematic word, is replaced: imbiBE GIN NERvously.
explanation.definitionFit: A beginner is someone new to an activity, which is exactly what a novice is.

clue.text: Dutch porter, namely one tucking into hard cheese

definitions.note: porter is the thematic word: read Dutch gin

indicators.note: something tucking into food goes inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: abbreviation of scilicet, Latin for namely
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A Dutch railway porter eating a lump of hard cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Porter, a dark beer, is the thematic word, so the definition is Dutch gin. SC for namely is the Latin scilicet; H as hard comes from pencil grades.
explanation.definitionFit: Schiedam is a Dutch town famous for distilling genever, and its name is used for the gin itself.

clue.text: Prolong second drink, when drinking where in Paris?

indicators.note: a drink is taken inside, so the drink word holds the French word

parts.note: a pint is a drink of beer

explanation.surface: Asking where in Paris you can make a second drink last longer.
explanation.walkthrough: The French word goes inside PINT between its N and T.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin out a task or a story is to drag it out and make it last longer.

clue.text: Imposing an unheralded beer upsets small taverns initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each word before it

parts.words: an unheralded beer upsets small taverns
parts.note: beer is the thematic word, read as gin, before the first letters are taken

explanation.surface: Pushing an unknown beer on drinkers annoys small pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Beer is a thematic word: with gin in its place the first letters spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: August as an adjective means grand and inspiring respect, which is what imposing means.

clue.text: Drink setter's Guinness, perhaps

definitions.note: Guinness is the thematic word: read gin, perhaps

parts.note: the setter speaks of what is his own

explanation.surface: Having a drink of the setter's stout.
explanation.walkthrough: Guinness, a stout, is a thematic word. Read 'gin, perhaps': gin rummy is one form of the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Rummy is a card game of which gin rummy is a well-known variety, so gin is an example.

clue.text: When drunk, tearfully sentimental female left home

explanation.surface: A woman who left home grows weepy over a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Maudlin describes self-pitying, tearful sentimentality, especially the kind brought on by too much drink.

clue.text: Things to be done, if a lawyer has inhaled dope

indicators.note: something inhaled is drawn inside, so one piece goes within the other

explanation.surface: A lawyer caught smoking cannabis has things to sort out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' suggests drugs but means information, GEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list of items to be dealt with, literally Latin for things to be done.

clue.text: Drink ouzo, then heave

parts.note: the thematic word, to be read as gin

explanation.surface: Knocking back ouzo and then being sick.
explanation.walkthrough: Ouzo, the Greek aniseed spirit, is a thematic word. 'Heave' hints at vomiting but means throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin sling is a cocktail of gin, sugar and water, usually with lemon.

clue.text: Fly high, having tackled fifth of puzzle from our setter

indicators.note: to tackle something is to take it on, so one word holds the other

parts.note: to soar is to fly high

indicators.note: the fifth of a word is its letter in position five

explanation.surface: Puck flies high after tackling part of his own crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our setter' looks like the compiler, but it is the sun, the setter in our sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Solar means coming from the sun, and the sun is the body that sets each evening.

clue.text: For this puzzle, liberal 12 27 is needed

indicators.note: a liberal reading is a free one, so the letters are freely rearranged

explanation.surface: Solving this needs a generous helping of brainpower.
explanation.walkthrough: The two unclued entries are the fodder, and the surface also says gin is needed liberally throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: This crossword is published in the Guardian's Genius series, the monthly prize puzzle.

clue.text: Country with small port

definitions.note: port is the thematic word: read gin

parts.note: a familiar name for the Netherlands

explanation.surface: A nation with a small harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like a harbour, but it is a thematic drink: read gin.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollands is an old name for Dutch gin, or genever, made in Holland.

clue.text: Fellow coming round with oddly dulled head

indicators.note: coming round means turning back, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college

indicators.note: oddly picks the letters in the odd-numbered places

parts.note: its first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A man regaining consciousness with a strangely dulled head.
explanation.definitionFit: Noddle is an old informal word for the head, especially as the seat of thought.

clue.text: Small fish added to prison dish

explanation.surface: Little fish thrown into a prison meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Stir is old British slang for prison, and fry are young fish just hatched.
explanation.definitionFit: A stir-fry is a dish of food cooked fast in hot oil in a wok while being stirred.

clue.text: Getting a double whisky ordered

indicators.note: ordered means put into an order, here a new arrangement of letters

parts.note: whisky is the thematic word, read as gin, and double means two of them

explanation.surface: Ordering a double whisky at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Whisky is a thematic word; read 'a double gin ordered'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaining means acquiring or obtaining something, so it matches getting as a present participle.
